newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Fuel oil up on tight supplies.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Fuel oil up on tight supplies.

text.p: Singapore fuel oil swaps firmed late afternoon on Tuesday with the front month May swaps trading above the $100 mark for the first time in about a month, traders said.
"Fuel oil is firmer because there is more confidence in the market that supplies are tightening," one trader said.
Front month May swaps were last quoted at $99.75/$101.00 per tonne up from Monday's $99.00/$99.50, brokers said.
May traded earlier in the day at $99.75 and $100.25, they said.

Traders said the market is picking up on expectations of tighter supplies due to the shutdown of several crude units in South Korea during the May-June period with exports from the Middle East to Singapore seen slowing down.
"Korean barrels are drying up abit for June," one trader said.

The re-emergence of China in the spot market has also boosted market confidence with one cargo sold recently at about $8.00 per barrel above spot Singapore quotes on a cost-and-freight basis, they said.
"The price is not so good but at least they (China) are buying," said a trader.
Gas oil swaps remained steady at at around the $25.00 per barrel mark with strong buying interest seen at this level, traders said.
May gas oil swaps were last quoted $25.10/$25.20 per barrel, unchanged from Monday's quotes. May traded earlier in the day at $25.07 and $25.10 per barrel, brokers said.
Traders said the market is trekking a steady downward course on the consistently lower bids by some traders.
The three traders, who have among them have bought more than 18 million barrels of gas oil since March 3, have slowly brought the bids down over the past month.
On Monday the bid was at $25.30 per barrel with one 150,000-barrel cargo traded at this level, down 20 cents from Friday's traded level.
